messages:
Alex Rivera: FYI I opened a PR to add an OPA pre-merge gate for infra changes that affect GPU pools + a freeze-window rule for eu-west. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/842
Maria Chen: quick question — does this block emergency fixes? we sometimes need hotfixes during windows.
Alex Rivera: good call. current plan is to enforce by default but provide an exception flow via ops-bot ticket + required auditors. exception creates a signed token that CI accepts.
Kevin O'Leary: cost note: the terraform change also bumps gpu-pool min size to 1 to avoid cold starts. that could add ~$8k/month depending on usage — can we make that opt-in?
Sophie Park: also worth calling out: helm values drift will still happen if people change values directly in clusters. do we have a weekly drift scan to reconcile?
ci-bot: [CI] opa/conftest: policy check failed for branch alex/opa-freeze. rule: freeze_window_violation (blocked)
ci-bot: Failure details:
```
policy: infra.freeze_window
message: "changes to gpu pools in eu-west during freeze window are disallowed"
resource: module.gpu_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu
```
Maria Chen: can we see the rego snippet? might help figure out edge cases (templated names, tag-only changes).
Alex Rivera: paste of the rego we added:
```
package infra.freeze_window

default deny = false

# deny if change touches a gpu pool in eu-west during frozen hours
deny[msg] {
  input.change.resource_type == "aws_autoscaling_group"
  startswith(input.change.name, "gpu-")
  input.change.region == "eu-west-1"
  time_hour := now_utc_hour()
  time_hour >= 0
  time_hour < 6
  msg = sprintf("freeze_window_violation: %s", [input.change.name])
}
```
Maria Chen: `now_utc_hour()` in CI isn't stable across runs unless we inject pipeline time. also what about tags-only updates? they shouldn't be blocked.
Kevin O'Leary: +1 to tags-only being allowed, we do frequent tag fixes. also prefer a "warn" mode at first so SREs can tune it.
Sophie Park: suggestion: add a repo-level config `infra/policies/config.yaml` with `freeze_mode: warn|enforce` and allow Conftest to read it. we can flip to enforce after 2 weeks.
Alex Rivera: OK I'll update the PR to add `freeze_mode` flag and make default `warn` for 14 days, then switch to `enforce`. I'll also add explicit logic to allow changes where only `tags` are modified.
Maria Chen: for exception flow, let's formalize runbook: ops-bot creates ticket -> on-call + infra lead must approve -> ticket generates an `infra-exception` artifact that CI validates. we should also audit exceptions monthly.
Sophie Park: and add ArgoCD webhook check: if a manual sync is performed during a freeze window, send a stern notification to #eng-oncall and create a drift alert.
Alex Rivera: noted. I'll stub the runbook and link it in the PR description. also will add unit tests for the rego rules.
ci-bot: [CI] updated checks will run once you push changes to the branch.
ops-bot: new exception flow stub created: https://ops.redwood/tickets/infra-exceptions/135 (draft)
Kevin O'Leary: sounds good. please ensure terraform plan output includes cost estimate or a pointer to the cost dashboard for reviewers.
Alex Rivera: will do. thanks all — updating the PR now: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/842 :thumbsup:
Sophie Park: thanks, Alex. can we add a short blurb to release notes so PMs know we have a freeze window?
Alex Rivera: yes — adding a note and an internal FAQ.
Maria Chen: leaving a review after Alex pushes the changes.
Alex Rivera: pushed update at 1764509999. CI triggered, will follow up with results.
